brief: Oil: refined-product cracks are at record highs relative to crude, which SG reads as crude under-pricing tightness rather than products overestimating it, because refining capacity (US refiners near record utilization, damaged Middle East and Russian capacity, China's export quotas) cannot convert available crude into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. Base case (50% probability, moderate conviction): a narrow US-Iran deal around the November 3 midterms plus fuller resolution by year-end eases the 193-day Hormuz disruption, taking Brent from around $100/bbl in September-October to $80/bbl by December 2026 and $77/bbl by late 2027. Stalemate (30%) keeps Brent near $130/bbl by December 2026. Escalation (20%) could push Brent toward $150/bbl. Gold: SG stays constructive through 2027, forecasting $4,750/oz by 4Q26 and an average annual price above $5,000/oz in 2027, driven by a weaker dollar and recovering central-bank, ETF and futures demand that increasingly offsets elevated real yields, whose historical correlation with gold broke down in August. Copper: SG raises its 4Q26 target to $14,750/t. COMEX-concentrated inventories mask tightness outside the US, AI and power-grid electrification lift demand, while a potential record-strength El Niño and DRC sulphuric-acid cost inflation threaten supply.
